source.title: Language-Triggered Value Inconsistencies in Multilingual LLMs
source.authors: Mauricio Neubecker; Maximilian Eder; Tim Würfl; J. Hoelscher-Obermaier; Jeyashree Krishnan; A. Rangarajan

record.tranche_reason: The study evaluates harmfulness across prompt languages, a different setting for safety behaviour from the fine-tuning and response-opening mechanisms in the claim. It reports its own language-comparison results, but does not test the claim versions.
record.gate_note: RQ3 measures harmfulness for harmful requests in English and Chinese. This is a related safety finding, but it does not test fine-tuning on harmful or benign data, first-token KL concentration, opening-token bypasses, localization in parameters, causes of shallowness, or deepening training. RQ1 and RQ2 concern value answers and identity cues, not the claim's safety mechanisms.
record.test_reason: The study measures how judged harmfulness on TRIDENT harmful requests differs between English and Chinese prompts. It does not fine-tune models (V1, V2) or measure per-token KL (V3). It does not prefill, add suffixes or change decoding (V4), localize safety in parameters (V5), test causes of shallowness (V6) or train deeper safety (V7). A prompt-language switch is not one of V4's named bypass routes. Qi et al. (2024), an original source, is cited only for the 1–5 harmfulness rubric, used as a measuring tool. The record's relation 'tests' / T3 contradicts its own reasoning and should be cites_only / T6.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase of the RQ3 safety result is accurate but leaves out the paper's main conclusions. Value answers shift with prompt language yet stay closer to US survey responses in every language. Answers track the prompt language rather than a stated user identity, which the authors read as language dominance, not sycophancy. Translator choice moves the measured value distributions by 82% of a language change, so raw cross-lingual distances are uninterpretable. On safety, they conclude most models are less safe in Chinese. In the 7–9B band the two Chinese-origin models are the exceptions; the gap persists at larger scale but the origin split does not. The direction is robust; per-model magnitude is not, because of truncation.
record.recipe_differences: The study does not fine-tune models or measure response-token KL, prefilling, or parameter localization; it evaluates harmfulness across prompt languages.
record.method_sensitivity: The authors report that Chinese answers hit the generation cap more often and that the truncation skew correlates with the harmfulness gap (ρ = +0.64, not significantly). Restricting to items without truncation preserves the effect for mistral, attenuates it for llama, puts gemma2-9b close to zero, and leaves too few untruncated items to check aya-expanse. The authors also report a translator-swap analysis on 146 items: the model ordering is preserved (ρ = +0.93), while each model's cross-rendering per-item agreement is ρ = 0.57–0.67.

fits_no_version.finding: Mean harmfulness of responses to the same TRIDENT harmful request is higher in Chinese than in English for 11 of 13 models (Table 8). In the 7–9B band the two Chinese-origin models are the exceptions: qwen2.5-7b Δ −0.161 and deepseek-7b Δ +0.003. Among the larger models, gemma3-27b reverses (Δ −0.318) and deepseek-v3 is near zero (Δ +0.037, CI covers zero). A translator swap on 146 items leaves the gap's ordering intact (ρ = +0.93), but the truncation skew correlates with Δ.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Prompt language changes the judged harmfulness of a safety-trained model's response to the same harmful request.

record.peer_reviewed: The Proceedings of the Workshop on Open Reasoning Across Cultures & Languages (ORACLE), 2026
record.problems: Chinese TRIDENT prompts are a single GPT-5.6 rendering and are not expert-validated. Chinese answers hit the generation cap more often, and the authors say this may make partially delivered answers score as more compliant. The untruncated-item analysis is limited for some models. The larger-model replication changes scale and measurement channel at once. There are no per-juror values in the reported table.
record.rows_left_out: None. RQ1 and RQ2 results on value answers and identity cues were left out because they do not measure the safety behaviour or mechanisms named in the claim.

untested.parts: Fine-tuning on harmful examples and resulting harmful compliance.
Fine-tuning on benign data and resulting harmful compliance.
Per-token KL between aligned and base models on harmful prompts.
Prefilling, adversarial suffixes or decoding changes to bypass refusal; prompt-language switching is not among these.
Localization of safety in a small set of weights or ranks.
Whether data or training objective causes shallow safety.
Deepening safety training and its robustness.

record.verdict_notes: All row links to ['none'] and the cannot_determine states are correct; row values match Table 8. Only the study-level relation and tranche need correcting, from tests/T3 to cites_only/T6. The study is about multilingual safety and value consistency, not shallow safety alignment. A possible new claim on language-dependent harmfulness is recorded under fits_no_version.

versions.untested_parts: Fine-tuning on harmful examples and its effect on refusal or harmful compliance.
Fine-tuning on benign data and its effect on harmful compliance.
Per-token KL divergence between aligned and base models on harmful prompts.
Prefilling, suffixes, or decoding changes as ways to bypass refusal.
Whether a small set of weights or ranks carries safety behaviour.
Whether training data or objectives cause safety shallowness.
Training that deepens safety behaviour and whether it is robust.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

relation.reason: Section 3.5 cites Qi et al. for the harmfulness rubric without testing or using the shallow-safety finding.

tranche.reason: The study evaluates language-dependent values and harmfulness; its results neither test nor use any of V1–V7.

source_check.notes: Table 8 itself reports aya-23 q=0.0504 and deepseek-v3 q=0.0072 despite the latter's CI spanning zero; these are not transcription errors. Section 4.3 cautions that translation and unequal truncation affect interpretation and per-model gap magnitudes.
